briefs.source_chain: Summer yield selloff is post-Covid normalisation, not fiscal, and coupon income is keeping bond returns from going outright negative -> last week energy (Hormuz stalemate) drove Brent/gas higher and pushed yields to multi-year highs -> that plus a strong payrolls print lifted Fed hike odds to 62% -> DB expects Friday CPI to confirm inflation near-unchanged and an ECB hike Thursday -> risk assets and credit softened on the week, AfD's Saxony-Anhalt result adds a political risk overlay.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: normalisation-not-fiscal yield framing with coupon cushion -> energy-driven yield/risk-asset moves last week (Hormuz, Brent, gas) -> payrolls lift Fed hike odds to 62% -> DB CPI/ECB forecasts -> AfD result -> Asia tech rally overnight with US closed for Labor Day.

briefs.source_chain: Global yields at multi-decade highs while VIX sits at cycle lows -> Friday's payrolls undercuts stagflation talk but Waller flags next week's CPI/PPI as the real test -> rate pressure has been a real headwind, so equity 'resilience' actually masks multiple de-rating against uniform earnings, with the discount-rate-vs-unsustainable-earnings question unresolved -> a selloff halt would be unequivocally bullish, but two unrelated drivers (geopolitical oil/gas repricing, debt-funded AI capex) keep pressuring rates -> momentum has reset ~50% with changed composition, so 1H leaders shouldn't lead 2H -> Wilson would add EU defense on the earnings/price divergence and expects rotation into AI use-case beneficiaries.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same order, same conclusions and the same 'unequivocally bullish if rates halt' pivot, same two unrelated bond drivers, same momentum-reset and EU-defense/AI-use-case calls.

briefs.source_chain: Last month's goldilocks call was wrong; a bond selloff has since hit yields, but rates markets still underprice tightening even as oil/gas/food inflation pressure builds -> so either inflation falls or rate pressure persists, and persistent rate pressure forces a risk-asset adjustment -> four dislocations: Fed pricing too shallow versus ISM prices-paid signal, ECB pricing flat despite hawkish data, oil curve assumes a Hormuz reopening that keeps not happening, and equities/credit remain complacent as real yields climb with fewer cushions (rate cuts, fiscal room) available -> conclusion: the current equilibrium is unsustainable.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: unsustainable equilibrium -> bond selloff to multi-year highs against still-shallow pricing -> Brent/gas/food inflation evidence -> the same either/or framing -> the same four dislocations with matching figures (60% hike odds, 74bps to 72bps ECB pricing, $83.2 six-month Brent, 70bps+ real yield rise) -> same conclusion.

distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the complacency call and its real-yield evidence are intact; the dropped analogues are corroboration.

briefs.source_chain: PJM and ERCOT both hit all-time peak demand records this summer, but only PJM prices reacted because ERCOT's load was covered by renewables/storage -> PJM's heat-wave peak (168/162 GW) beat its 2006 record and forecast with $2,000+/MWh spikes, and forwards held strong -> ERCOT's 91 GW record beat last year and forecast but priced only in the low hundreds, and its forwards have since weakened further on Abbott's Batch Zero pause, pushing the curve into contango -> elsewhere MISO matched forecast while New England/NY/CA undershot -> record Q2 gas turbine orders (38 GW, +71% YoY) confirm the demand buildout -> Wolfe holds sentiment flat at '2', flagging the PJM RBP cost-allocation risk (pending FERC) against improving CEG tone and the cleared Vistra/Cogentrix deal.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and same figures throughout (168/162 GW, 154 GW forecast, $2,000/MWh, 159 GW/$1,000/MWh, 91 GW record, contango after Abbott's letter, 38 GW/+71% turbine orders, sentiment flat at '2', RBP risk vs. CEG tone and cleared Cogentrix deal).
